seo.title: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Ottawa - No Home Help
seo.description: Current Ottawa contacts for emergency shelter, meals, day services, health care, benefits, jobs, legal help and specialist support.

page.heading: Homeless and housing-crisis help in Ottawa
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious injury, overdose, fire or a crime in progress: call 911. Shelter placement and City financial assistance: call 311. Food and community-service referrals: call 211.
page.notice: Shelters and services can be full, change hours or require an assessment or referral. Call before travelling whenever possible. No listing guarantees a bed, housing, treatment, benefit, payment or job.
page.intro: If one shelter is full, call 311 and try the other local services below. Say who needs help, your age, whether children or a pet are with you, and any urgent health, safety, accessibility or language needs. Ask about overflow, day programs, outreach and the next safe option rather than relying on one address.
page.footer: No Home Help is independent of the City and service providers. Information was checked against official provider or government pages; report a change if a number, address or access rule is no longer correct.

entries.title: 911 — emergency services
entries.description: Call for immediate danger, serious injury, suspected overdose, fire or a crime in progress. Give the exact address or nearest intersection and explain the immediate risk.
entries.how_to_access: Call 911. For a non-emergency police matter, Ottawa Police can be reached at 613-236-1222.

entries.title: City of Ottawa — emergency shelter access
entries.description: The City coordinates placement into adult, youth and family emergency shelters. Shelter stays may include meals, case management and housing support. Capacity changes, and a call does not guarantee a bed.
entries.how_to_access: Call 311 and ask for emergency housing. Say whether you are an adult, youth or family and describe accessibility, health and safety needs. Ask for overflow and a day-program alternative if no suitable space is immediately available.

entries.title: 211 Ontario — community and social-service referrals
entries.description: A navigator can search for nearby food, free meals, health care, housing, financial help, Indigenous services, newcomer support and other community programs. The service is free and confidential and can provide more than one option.
entries.hours: Phone and text: 24 hours; online chat hours vary
entries.how_to_access: Call or text 211. The Ottawa-area number is 613-761-9076 and the toll-free number is 1-877-330-3213. Ask the navigator to check current eligibility and hours.

entries.title: Health811 Ontario — non-emergency health advice
entries.description: Speak with a registered nurse about a non-emergency health problem and get guidance about appropriate care. This is not an ambulance or emergency service.
entries.how_to_access: Call 811. Call 911 instead for a life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: The Ottawa Mission — emergency shelter for men
entries.description: Emergency shelter for adult men, with meals, clothing, health care, housing support, education, employment and addiction services. Availability is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call the Mission and call 311 for current placement advice. Ask staff what time new-arrival intake begins and what alternative is available if full.

entries.title: Shepherds of Good Hope — all-gender shelter services
entries.description: Separate shelter services include a men's shelter, women's shelter and transitional emergency program. The organization also provides health, harm-reduction and housing supports.
entries.hours: Call for current intake and availability
entries.how_to_access: Call 311 for referral to an appropriate available shelter. Shepherds lists extensions 2101 for the transitional emergency program, 2200 for the men's shelter and 2300 for the women's shelter.

entries.title: Salvation Army Ottawa Booth Centre — shelter for men
entries.description: Emergency shelter for adult men, plus meals, clothing, counselling, case management, referrals and addiction-related programs. Capacity changes.
entries.how_to_access: Call 311 for current shelter placement or call the Booth Centre before travelling. Ask about intake, accessibility and an alternative if full.

entries.title: Cornerstone Housing for Women — emergency shelter
entries.description: Emergency shelter and housing support for women and gender-diverse people experiencing homelessness or housing crisis. Call directly to confirm eligibility and space.
entries.hours: Call for current intake and availability
entries.how_to_access: Call the emergency shelter and also ask 311 about the most appropriate available placement. Do not rely on the head-office number for shelter intake.

entries.title: YSB — Young Women's Emergency Shelter
entries.description: Youth Services Bureau emergency shelter for young women and gender-diverse youth, with meals, counselling and help toward housing, education, work and training. YSB's current housing program generally serves ages 16 to 20.
entries.how_to_access: Call the shelter directly; YSB lists extension 225 for the Young Women's Shelter. Confirm age eligibility and current availability.

entries.title: YSB — Young Men's Emergency Shelter
entries.description: Youth Services Bureau emergency shelter for young men and gender-diverse youth, with meals, counselling and help toward housing, education, work and training. YSB's current housing program generally serves ages 16 to 20.
entries.how_to_access: Call the shelter directly. Confirm age eligibility and current availability; ask about shelter diversion or another youth option if no bed is open.

entries.title: Housing Registry of Ottawa — subsidized and supportive housing
entries.description: Help applying for rent-geared-to-income, affordable or supportive housing. The Registry does not provide emergency shelter and warns that subsidized-housing waits can exceed five years, so keep using immediate housing supports while an application is active.
entries.address: 240 Catherine Street, Suite 110, Ottawa, ON K2P 2G8
entries.hours: Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 08:30–16:30; Tuesday 13:00–16:30
entries.how_to_access: Call for help completing or updating an application, or collect a paper form at the office. Keep contact details current and update the application at least annually.

entries.title: The Ottawa Mission — community meals
entries.description: Free community meals are offered to people who are not staying in the shelter. Published serving times are breakfast 08:00–08:30, lunch 11:20–12:00 and dinner 15:00–15:30; times can change.
entries.how_to_access: Meals are available to the wider community. Call before a long journey because serving arrangements and capacity can change.

entries.title: Shepherds of Good Hope — community kitchen and evening drop-in
entries.description: Meals and a low-barrier drop-in open to everyone. The provider publishes breakfast 07:00–08:00, lunch 11:00–12:30, dinner 16:00–17:30, and a sandwich or leftover meal from 18:00–21:00.
entries.address: Richcraft Hope Centre, 216 Murray Street, Ottawa, ON
entries.hours: Drop-in 07:00–23:00 every day; meal times are listed on the provider page
entries.how_to_access: Walk in. Call ahead if travelling far or if you need accessibility information.

entries.title: Ottawa Food Bank — find the program serving your area
entries.description: The official lookup tool identifies the community food program assigned to an Ottawa address and shows its latest published hours. Food programs may ask for identification or proof of address and may have service limits.
entries.address: Use the online lookup for the correct local program
entries.how_to_access: Enter your current address in the lookup tool or call for help finding the correct program. Confirm required documents and hours before travelling.

entries.title: Belong Ottawa at St Luke's Table — breakfast and lunch
entries.description: A welcoming day program offering coffee, tea, breakfast, lunch, hygiene supplies, phone access, Wi-Fi, computers and community support.
entries.address: Monday–Friday: 211 Bronson Avenue; Saturday: 70 James Street, Ottawa, ON
entries.hours: Check the current program calendar or call
entries.how_to_access: Walk in during service hours. Confirm the day's location and meal time before travelling.

entries.title: Belong Ottawa — three day programs
entries.description: Centre 454, The Well and St Luke's Table offer combinations of meals, showers, laundry, hygiene supplies, phone access, computers, Wi-Fi, referrals and community activities. Services and eligibility differ by location.
entries.address: Centre 454: 454 King Edward Avenue; The Well entrance: 275 Elgin Street; St Luke's Table: 211 Bronson Avenue, Ottawa, ON
entries.hours: Varies by location and service; check the current calendar
entries.how_to_access: Choose the location for the service you need and call before travelling. The Well has designated service hours for women and gender-diverse people.

entries.title: Centre 454 — showers, laundry and basic needs
entries.description: Belong Ottawa day program with meals, showers, laundry, supplies, phone and internet access, referrals and community support.
entries.address: 454 King Edward Avenue, Ottawa, ON K1N 7M8
entries.hours: Check the current location page or call
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling to confirm shower and laundry availability, sign-up procedure and the last service time.

entries.title: The Well — showers, laundry and computers
entries.description: Inclusive day program offering meals, laundry, showers, computers and activities, with designated service hours for women and gender-diverse people.
entries.address: Entrance at 275 Elgin Street, Ottawa, ON
entries.hours: Check the current location page or call
entries.how_to_access: Call to confirm the day's eligibility and sign-up times for showers or laundry before travelling.

entries.title: The Ottawa Mission — clothing and basic supplies
entries.description: The Mission lists food, shelter and clothing among its emergency services. Stock and sizes depend on donations and are not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Ask the front desk or client-services team what is available and whether another clothing program can help if the item or size is unavailable.

entries.title: Centretown Community Health Centre — Urban Health Program
entries.description: Walk-in physical and mental health care for people who are unhoused or unstably housed and do not have a family doctor, subject to triage and catchment rules. Services include chronic and preventive care, harm-reduction supplies, showers, ID replacement and navigation. People without OHIP may qualify.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in for triage or call to discuss eligibility and an appointment. This is not emergency care; call 911 for a life-threatening emergency.

entries.title: YSB Youth Health Clinic — no health card required
entries.description: Free walk-in primary health care for street-involved youth ages 16 to 24, including minor injuries and illness, referrals and preventive dental care. A health card is not required.
entries.hours: Nurse practitioner Monday–Wednesday 12:30–16:30 and Friday 12:30–16:00; dental most Fridays 12:30–16:30
entries.how_to_access: Walk in; appointments are first come, first served. Text the published clinic number or call 613-241-7913 extension 222 to confirm the current schedule.

entries.title: 988 Suicide Crisis Helpline
entries.description: Call or text for immediate suicide-crisis support. It is available across Canada in English and French. Call 911 if there is immediate danger or urgent medical need.
entries.how_to_access: Call or text 988.

entries.title: AccessMHA — mental-health and addiction navigation
entries.description: Free starting point for people age 16 or older seeking mental-health, substance-use or addiction services in eastern Ontario. A trained worker assesses needs and connects the person to a partner service. AccessMHA is not a crisis service.
entries.how_to_access: Self-refer online and choose a callback time, or call for help with the form. For an emergency or immediate risk, call 911 or go to an emergency department.

entries.title: Rapid Access Addiction Medicine clinic
entries.description: Low-barrier assessment and treatment for concerns about alcohol or opioid use. No medical referral is required; virtual access may be available.
entries.address: The Royal Ottawa Mental Health Centre, 1145 Carling Avenue, Ottawa, ON K1Z 7K4
entries.hours: Call extension 6508 or check the current clinic listing
entries.how_to_access: Call 613-722-6521 extension 6508 to confirm the current walk-in or virtual schedule. This is not an emergency service.

entries.title: YSB — youth crisis line and chat
entries.description: Immediate crisis support for youth in Ottawa and eastern Ontario. The service can listen, assess the situation and connect a young person to appropriate help.
entries.how_to_access: Call 613-260-2360, toll-free 1-877-377-7775, or use the live crisis chat. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Centre 507 — adult drop-in open 22 hours daily
entries.description: Adult drop-in with healthy meals, a safe indoor place, community and connections to resources. It is not an overnight shelter, but its long daily opening hours can provide an alternative place to ask for help when other programs are closed.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in or call to confirm the service you need. Call 311 for an emergency shelter referral.

entries.title: Catherine Street Community Service Hub
entries.description: Accessible walk-in hub with a safe indoor resting area, washrooms, charging, public computers, Wi-Fi and telephones. Staff and partners can help with crisis referrals, housing, financial assistance, food, employment and health services.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in or call extension 26468. Some partner services follow separate schedules, so ask the reception desk what is available that day.

entries.title: Free phone, Wi-Fi and computers at day programs
entries.description: St Luke's Table publishes free phone, Wi-Fi and computer access. Belong Ottawa's other locations and the Catherine Street hub also list communication or computer access; availability depends on program hours.
entries.address: St Luke's Table: 211 Bronson Avenue; Catherine Street hub: 370 Catherine Street, Ottawa, ON
entries.how_to_access: Ask reception about device charging, a computer or making an outgoing call. Never leave a phone unattended.

entries.title: OC Transpo EquiPass — reduced fares for low-income residents
entries.description: Discounted single-ride and monthly transit fares for eligible low-income Ottawa residents. ODSP recipients use the Community Pass instead. Prices and income thresholds can change.
entries.how_to_access: Check current eligibility and documents before applying. Ask an Ontario Works or community-service worker for help if identification or proof of income is a barrier.

entries.title: Ontario Works — income and employment assistance
entries.description: Provincial financial assistance for eligible people in need, with employment and health-related benefits. Applications require an assessment and approval is not guaranteed.
entries.address: City Employment and Social Services centres or online
entries.how_to_access: Apply online or by phone. For an urgent same-day need, if under 18 and not living with parents, or if caring for a child you are not legally required to support, call 311 and select Community and Social Services.

entries.title: City outreach workers at shelters and day programs
entries.description: City case workers visit community locations to help with Ontario Works, emergency assistance, essential health supports, ODSP connections, housing, employment and other referrals. This can be easier than reaching a central office.
entries.address: Regular visits include The Ottawa Mission, Shepherds of Good Hope, Booth Centre, Centre 454, The Well and St Luke's Table
entries.hours: Location schedule published on the City page; call because schedules can change
entries.how_to_access: Check the City's current walk-in table or call 311 Monday–Friday 08:30–16:00 and select Community and Social Services.

entries.title: Emergency Assistance — temporary financial support
entries.description: Short-term help for eligible Ontario residents facing an emergency such as eviction, abuse, safety risk, serious health crisis, fire, flood or theft. People already receiving Ontario Works or ODSP are not eligible for this separate program.
entries.address: Apply online or through City Employment and Social Services
entries.hours: Employment and Social Services centres Monday–Friday 08:00–16:30
entries.how_to_access: Read the eligibility rules and apply online. Call 311 and select Community and Social Services if you lack a SIN, email or phone, need an interpreter, or need help with the application.

entries.title: Employment Ontario at the City of Ottawa
entries.description: Free help with job searching, résumés, interviews, skills and career planning. The resource centre provides computers, Wi-Fi and job-search tools.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in, email EOottawa@ottawa.ca or call extension 14372. Ask about training or transport supports if these are barriers to work.

entries.title: YSB Employment Services — three Ottawa centres
entries.description: Free job-search, placement, training, certification and career support, with locations in south/east, west and east Ottawa. Services are especially relevant to youth but current eligibility should be confirmed.
entries.address: 1355 Bank Street, Suite 703; 301 Moodie Drive, Suite 203; or 2339 Ogilvie Road, Suite 24
entries.how_to_access: Call the nearest centre. West Ottawa: 613-688-0440. East Ottawa: 343-371-7791. Confirm eligibility and appointment requirements.

entries.title: Government of Canada Job Bank
entries.description: Official national job search, training and labour-market information. It is a useful additional search tool but does not replace local employment support and does not guarantee work.
entries.how_to_access: Use a public computer at the Catherine Street hub, Belong Ottawa or an employment centre if you do not have internet access.

entries.title: Community Legal Services of Ottawa
entries.description: Free legal services for eligible low-income Ottawa residents in housing law for tenants, public benefits, immigration and refugee law. Three offices serve different areas of the city.
entries.address: Downtown: 1 Nicholas Street, Suite 422; South: 1355 Bank Street, Suite 406; West: 1299 Richmond Road, Ottawa, ON
entries.hours: Call for intake hours and area eligibility
entries.how_to_access: Call and describe the legal problem, deadline, income and current address or shelter area. The clinic may refer you to the office serving your area.

entries.title: Housing Help — eviction prevention and tenant support
entries.description: Free housing advocacy and practical support for low- and moderate-income residents in west Ottawa, including help with landlord disputes and preventing housing loss.
entries.address: 1335 Carling Avenue, Unit 214, Ottawa, ON K1Z 8N8
entries.how_to_access: Call as early as possible if there is an eviction notice or hearing date. Bring or photograph the lease, notices and relevant messages if available.

entries.title: Action Housing — eviction prevention and tenant support
entries.description: Free housing advocacy and practical support for low- and moderate-income residents in east Ottawa, including help with landlord disputes and preventing housing loss.
entries.address: 214 Montreal Road, Unit 202, Ottawa, ON K1L 8L8
entries.how_to_access: Call as early as possible if there is an eviction notice or hearing date. French service is available through Action Logement.

entries.title: Centretown Community Health Centre — ID replacement support
entries.description: The Urban Health Program lists practical help with replacing identification for eligible people who are unhoused or unstably housed. A social-services walk-in can also help with forms and service navigation.
entries.hours: Urban Health walk-in Tuesday and Friday 09:00–11:30; call for ID-clinic details
entries.how_to_access: Call before travelling and ask specifically about the next ID replacement clinic, eligibility and any documents or guarantor information to bring.

entries.title: Interval House of Ottawa — crisis line and emergency shelter
entries.description: Emergency shelter and safety support for women, femmes, Two Spirit, non-binary and gender-expansive people, with dependants and pets. The address is confidential. Outreach and transitional support may be available when shelter living is not possible or desired.
entries.how_to_access: Call the crisis line for support or current shelter space. For text-only crisis support or shelter space, use 613-704-5535. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: Oshki Kizis Lodge — Indigenous women and children fleeing violence
entries.description: Minwaashin Lodge's 25-bed Indigenous-specific shelter offers 24-hour residential support, advocacy, counselling, housing help, referrals, legal advocacy and cultural and spiritual programs for First Nations, Inuit and Métis women and children fleeing abuse.
entries.address: 2323 St. Laurent Boulevard, Ottawa, ON K1G 4J8
entries.how_to_access: Call the crisis line before travelling to confirm safety, eligibility, accessibility and space. Call 911 for immediate danger.

entries.title: YSB Downtown Services and Drop-in — youth
entries.description: Safe day space for youth experiencing homelessness or poverty, with meals, showers, laundry, clothing, phone and internet, a food bank, housing help, crisis support and links to health care.
entries.how_to_access: Walk in and ask reception for the service needed. Current programs focus on youth roughly ages 16 to 20 or 24 depending on the service; call extension 300 to confirm.

entries.title: Centretown CHC — social-services walk-in
entries.description: First-come, first-served help with forms, housing, finances, food security, health navigation, mental-health and addiction connections, rapid HIV testing and crisis support.
entries.hours: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday; registration at 12:45, clinic 13:00–16:00
entries.how_to_access: No appointment is required, but the clinic closes when all places are filled. Arrive before registration and call to confirm the schedule.

entries.title: Veterans Affairs Canada — homelessness and emergency support
entries.description: Veterans and eligible family members can ask about case management, housing support and the Veterans Emergency Fund for urgent essentials such as food, clothing, uninsured medical costs or shelter. Every application is assessed; funding is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call and state that you are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Ask what proof of identity or service is needed and what immediate support is possible.

entries.title: VETS Canada — Ottawa drop-in and support centre
entries.description: Local support for Canadian veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The federal Veterans Affairs directory lists this Ottawa centre as a community support option.
entries.how_to_access: Call toll-free and ask for the Ottawa centre. Confirm current hours and what service or documents are needed.

entries.title: Community Veterinary Outreach — Ottawa clinics
entries.description: Veterinary care, pet food or supplies and human-health connections for people who are homeless or vulnerably housed. Ottawa clinics operate through partner agencies and are not a walk-in veterinary emergency service.
entries.address: Clinics rotate among Ottawa partner agencies
entries.how_to_access: Ask a shelter, outreach worker or partner agency for a referral and the next clinic date. Check eligibility before attending.

entries.title: Interval House — pet-inclusive violence shelter
entries.description: The emergency shelter has separate housing for dogs, cats and other small pets so eligible survivors do not have to choose between safety and leaving a pet behind. Shelter space is not guaranteed.
entries.how_to_access: Call the crisis line and explain what animals are with you and any urgent safety needs. Ask what supplies, vaccination information or transport may be required.
